proposal: Recalibrate the golf:pga-tour coverage contract (authority.json) from horizonDays 14 → 21 so its ONE legitimate season pause stops firing a false high-severity contract-breach every static-pipeline run. PGA Tour has a ~2.5-week gap between the TOUR Championship (~30 Aug) and the FedExCup Fall opener (2026: Biltmore Championship 17–20 Sep, after Procore was dropped); with a 14-day horizon the WP-243 contract mechanism reported golf:pga-tour BREACHED (high severity — the one gap class defined as a broken promise) on every run through that ~18-day window, even though golf coverage was actually complete (Biltmore already boarded, plus DP World Tour every week). 21 days spans the pause; the rest of the season is weekly, so the promise (≥1 event in horizon) is unchanged in practice. The note documents why this contract's horizon differs from DP World Tour's 14. Single-value config tune of an existing mechanism; touches no protected path.
evidence: coverage-audit.json (2026-08-31 10:34Z) sourceIssues[0]: coverage-critic web-verified the breach as a FALSE positive — 'FALSK contract-breach … det finnes en LEGITIM sesongpause mellom TOUR Championship (~30 aug) og FedExCup Fall-åpningen (Biltmore 17.–20. sep) … Biltmore 17. sep ER allerede boardet, så golf-dekningen er faktisk komplett.' Its explicit recommendation: 'øk horizonDays for golf:pga-tour til ~21 ELLER legg inn en kjent-pause-unntak.' Also restated in the audit notes.

research-log.json (2026-08-30 22:45Z): the research agent hand-boarded Biltmore to answer the breach and flagged the standing miscalibration — 'PGA Tour has a ~2.5-week gap between the FedExCup finale (30 Aug) and the FedExCup Fall opener … the 14-day contract window can't see season structure.' Two independent agents diagnosed the same false breach.

coverage-contracts.json (2026-08-31 11:20Z): golf:pga-tour upcoming=0 status=breached; breached:['golf:pga-tour'] — the false high-severity gap materialised in the published data, polluting the WP-243 contracts port in port-report.json and consuming coverage-critic/research triage every run.

Simulated the fix against live events.json at now=2026-08-31 11:20Z via scripts/lib/coverage-contracts.js assessContracts: horizon=14 → upcoming=0 status=breached; horizon=21 → upcoming=1 status=met, breached=[] (Biltmore Championship, tournament 'PGA Tour', now falls in the window and is counted; no other contract changes).
npm test: 1525 passed (87 files) — the change is config-only (authority.schema still validates; authority-schema.test.js only pins the known competition id set).
notes: Chose the horizon bump over a new known-pause-exception schema field: the v2 bias is sharpen-what-exists over new machinery, and a single number the domain-expert audit web-verified and endorsed (~21) is the smallest defensible change. An exception window would add a schema field + lib branch + tests for a once-a-year, one-competition case.

Why 21 specifically: on the morning after the finale the next PGA fixture is 17 days out; 21 spans it with margin while staying tight enough that the promise still has teeth (weekly the rest of the season). If a future year's fall opener lands >21 days out it will re-breach — a fresh evidenced signal, not silently masked.

How we'll know it worked: coverage-contracts.json golf:pga-tour returns to status 'met', the false high gap stops appearing in coverage-gaps.json / port-report contracts port, and coverage-critic/research stop spending a triage note on it each run. DP World Tour (also golf) is untouched — it keeps horizon 14 and stayed 'met'.

Did not touch the standing 'no wholesale golf/Serie A/EL fetcher' item (self-repair-owned, bigger, adds machinery) — this run fixes the misfiring threshold with the clearest evidence, per one-improvement-per-run.
